answer: Python is a beginner-friendly, general-purpose language. It uses indentation to group code. For example: `for name in ["Ada", "Lin"]: print(name)` loops over two names. Start with variables, conditions, loops, functions, and small projects.

Java is a strongly typed, object-oriented language that runs on the Java Virtual Machine. A variable declares its type, for example `int score = 10;`. A Java program typically puts code inside a class and starts from `public static void main(String[] args)`.

A linked list stores values in nodes. Each node points to the next node; a doubly linked list also points to the previous one. Unlike an array, nodes do not need adjacent memory. Inserting after a known node is quick, but finding the node at position 20 requires walking from the head.

An array stores items in order, and each item is accessed by an index. In most languages indexing starts at 0, so the first item is `items[0]`. Reading or updating by index is fast; inserting in the middle may require shifting later items.

A loop repeats a block of code. Use a `for` loop when you know the items or number of repetitions; use a `while` loop when you want to continue until a condition changes. Example: `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++)` runs three times. Make sure a `while` loop can eventually stop.

A function is a named, reusable block of code. It can accept inputs (parameters) and return a result. Example: `function double(n) { return n * 2; }` can be called as `double(4)` and returns `8`. In Java, functions defined inside a class are usually called methods.

Object-oriented programming (OOP) organizes code around objects. A class describes shared data and behavior; an object is one instance of that class. For example, a `Book` class might have a `title` field and a `open()` method. Encapsulation keeps related state and behavior together; inheritance and polymorphism help model related types.

Git is a version-control tool that records snapshots of your files. A simple workflow is: `git status` to inspect changes, `git add <file>` to stage them, then `git commit -m "Describe the change"` to save a snapshot. A branch lets you work on a change separately before merging it.

GitHub hosts Git repositories online and adds collaboration tools. Git tracks changes on your computer; GitHub stores and shares repositories. You can clone a repo, make a branch, push your commits, and open a pull request so others can review the change. Use the GitHub Explorer to search public repositories.
